events.body:
## Outcome

Users can understand what will always remain free and portable, what ForkMesh sells, and how paid services sustain the network without control of the protocol.

## Scope

- Separate the free protocol and self-hostable software from paid hosting, team administration, indexing, reliability, support, and infrastructure.
- Publish initial plans, usage units, portability commitments, support boundaries, and an explicit no-data-sale policy.
- Model acquisition, service costs, gross margin, and the path from public-project value to paid adoption.

## Acceptance criteria

- A public entitlement matrix clearly distinguishes protocol rights, self-hosted capabilities, free hosted limits, and paid services.
- Pricing interviews validate buyer, budget, and top paid jobs with documented revisions.
- Unit-economics instrumentation exists before any unlimited paid plan launches.
- Linked automated evidence covers supported platforms, failure paths, rollback/recovery, documentation, and telemetry before closure.

## Delivery and dependencies

- Portfolio tier: **P0 release gate**
- Milestone: **Product contract & measurement**
- Numeric priority: **2 of 44** (1 is highest)
- Depends on: #476
- Assignee: unassigned until an accountable owner accepts the epic; fund independently releasable child issues rather than this umbrella epic.

## Progress baseline

**15% as of 2026-07-22.** The README names aligned revenue directions and the network already hosts services, but no simple entitlement/pricing model or measured unit economics is published. Progress may not exceed 85% without end-to-end validation or 95% without security, documentation, telemetry, and rollout evidence.

## Verification and measures

Primary measures: Pricing comprehension, qualified demand, trial-to-paid conversion, service cost, and infrastructure margin. Closure requires linked test runs, operational evidence, and current user-facing documentation.
